record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Find good heuristics to compute candidates for ques- tion 1.6.15.5.

evidence.quote: Find good heuristics to compute candidates for ques- tion 1.6.15.5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let A be a finite alphabet and let E be a separate alphabet of pattern variables. A pattern is a non-empty word p ∈ E*. A morphism h : E* → A* is non-erasing if h(x) is a non-empty word for every variable x ∈ E. Two finite words u, v ∈ A* are abelian equivalent, written u ~_ab v, if they have the same length and, for every letter a ∈ A, the number of occurrences of a in u equals the number of occurrences of a in v. A word w ∈ A* is said to encounter the pattern p in the abelian sense if there exist a non-erasing morphism h : E* → A* and a factorization w = w₀ h(p₁)' h(p₂)' ⋯ h(p_n)' w₁ where p = p₁ p₂ ⋯ p_n (with p_i ∈ E) and each h(p_i)' ~_ab h(p_i) and, for every two occurrences of the same variable, the corresponding factors are abelian equivalent. Otherwise w avoids p in the abelian sense. A pattern p is abelian k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over an alphabet of size k that avoids p in the abelian sense; p is abelian-avoidable if it is abelian k-avoidable for some k.

Problem. Provide effective heuristic procedures that, given a pattern p ∈ E* whose abelian avoidability status is unknown, produce candidate witnesses for either side of the question, namely:
(i) candidate finite or eventually periodic infinite words over a small alphabet (and candidate morphisms generating such words) that plausibly avoid p in the abelian sense, suitable for verification by direct computation up to a chosen length; and
(ii) candidate short factors or unavoidable abelian configurations that would prove p is abelian-unavoidable, suitable for a finite case analysis.

The heuristics should be efficient enough to be run on patterns of length at most a fixed modest bound and on alphabet sizes k ∈ {2, 3, 4}, and should improve substantially over exhaustive enumeration.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of patterns with respect to abelian avoidability remains incomplete: only a partial classification of short patterns (length ≤ 7 over few variables) and of binary patterns is known, and no general decision procedure or systematic heuristic for producing avoidance/unavoidance candidates has been established. Recent works (e.g., on abelian-2-avoidability of binary patterns and on abelian/additive powers in rich words, 2016–2024) continue to use ad-hoc computer search, indicating the heuristic question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Every Binary Pattern of Length Greater Than 14 Is Abelian-2-Avoidable
status_evidence.snippet: Best known upper bound on the length of abelian-2-unavoidable binary patterns reduced to 14; lower bound is 7.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of abelian-avoidable binary patterns still has a gap (lengths between the lower and upper bounds), showing the underlying decision problem is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Abelian pattern avoidance in partial words
status_evidence.snippet: A short list of four-letter patterns for which abelian avoidance is undecided is given.
status_evidence.claim: There remain explicit short patterns whose abelian avoidability is open, motivating the need for heuristics to compute candidates.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding abelian and additive powers in rich words
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) study of abelian-power avoidance in structured infinite words.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research uses ad-hoc constructions rather than a unified heuristic framework.
